questions.q: What does a Role by itself actually grant, before any RoleBinding exists?
options: Full cluster-admin access to everyone
Nothing — a Role defines permission rules but grants nothing to anyone until it's bound to a subject
Read access to every namespace automatically
Access only to the user who created it
questions.explain: A Role is just a set of rules (apiGroups, resources, verbs). It takes effect for a subject only once a RoleBinding attaches it to a User, Group, or ServiceAccount.

questions.q: Priya has a RoleBinding granting pod-reader (get/list/watch on pods) in the analytics namespace only. What can she do in the checkout namespace?
options: The same get/list/watch on Pods, since Roles apply cluster-wide by default
Nothing — the RoleBinding is scoped to analytics, so she has no permissions in checkout
Full admin access, since RBAC defaults to allow
She can delete Pods but not read them
questions.explain: A RoleBinding only grants its Role's permissions within the namespace the RoleBinding itself lives in. It has no effect in any other namespace.

questions.q: When should Northbridge's platform team use a ClusterRole + ClusterRoleBinding instead of per-namespace Roles?
options: Never — ClusterRole is deprecated
Only for Secrets, never for Pods
When the same permission (e.g. read Pods for on-call troubleshooting) needs to apply across every namespace at once, instead of creating one Role per namespace
Only when working with StatefulSets
questions.explain: ClusterRole + ClusterRoleBinding is the right tool when a permission should span the whole cluster rather than being repeated namespace by namespace.

questions.q: In a Role's rule `apiGroups: [""], resources: ["pods"], verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]`, what does the empty string in apiGroups mean?
options: The rule applies to no resources at all
It refers to the core API group, which includes Pods, Services, ConfigMaps, and Secrets
It is a syntax error that Kubernetes ignores
It grants access to every apiGroup, including custom resources
questions.explain: The core Kubernetes API group (Pods, Services, ConfigMaps, Secrets, Namespaces, etc.) is referenced with an empty string "" in apiGroups.

questions.q: Which command lets you directly verify whether a specific user can perform a specific action, without them having to try it first?
options: kubectl get rolebindings
kubectl describe role pod-reader
kubectl auth can-i <verb> <resource> --namespace <ns> --as <user>
kubectl apply -f role.yaml --dry-run
questions.explain: kubectl auth can-i, combined with --as to impersonate a user, answers exactly whether that user is permitted to perform a given verb on a given resource in a given namespace.
